name: PianoFrozenFinger
summary: A frozen-bubble technique for dense scenes: a fist freezes the hand-controlled bubble, and the user picks the target by pressing the matching coloured key on a small virtual piano that travels with the hand.
howItWorks: With the palm open, a transparent bubble and a small virtual piano move with the hand; the bubble captures several nearby targets, each matched in colour to a piano key. Clenching the fist freezes both the bubble and the piano (Single-Hand Frozen Gestures), so the hand can drop to the keys without moving the bubble. Pressing the key with the target's colour selects it; opening the palm unfreezes them. The number of keys can be adapted to the scene. In a 16-participant study (Vive Pro with a Leap Motion) selecting small atoms in dense clusters, LiftFrozenFinger raised the success rate by 15.71% and PianoFrozenFinger by 34.29% over MultiFingerBubble, with less hand fatigue; both were slower than MultiFingerBubble, PianoFrozenFinger was more accurate than LiftFrozenFinger, and 12 of 16 participants ranked it first.
advantages: Highest success rate of the four techniques tested, and the most preferred.
Pressing keys is a familiar, low-effort finger motion; the piano can hold more than three candidates.
limitations: Needs the piano to stay frozen; without SHFG the palm drops when pressing keys.
Tested only on near targets in a molecule-like scene.

relationships.note: Adds the fist freeze and a piano-key aid for picking within the bubble.
34.29% higher success rate and less fatigue, but slower.
Same SHFG freeze, different finger action.
